basics.name: Ciem Cornelissen
basics.label: PhD Researcher in Computer Science Engineering
basics.summary: PhD researcher in Computer Science Engineering at IDLab (Ghent University - imec), working on multi-modal self-supervised representation learning for autonomous perception. I develop transformer-based methods for learning unified representations from RGB, LiDAR, thermal, and other sensor streams, with broader research interests in predictive representations and world models.

work.name: IDLab, Ghent University - imec
work.summary: Research on multi-modal self-supervised representation learning and efficient sensor fusion for autonomous perception, with earlier work in hyperspectral imaging and precision agriculture.
highlights: Developed Le MuMo JEPA, a multi-modal self-supervised framework for unified RGB-LiDAR-thermal representations, accepted at the CVPR 2026 URVIS Workshop
Designed learnable fusion tokens as an efficient latent bottleneck and evaluated frozen representations on Waymo, nuScenes, and FLIR for depth, segmentation, and 3D detection
Developed LISA for illumination-invariant hyperspectral learning and OHSLIC for efficient UAV-based phenotype segmentation
Published in CVPR Workshops, IEEE Internet of Things Journal, WACV Workshops, and Neural Computing and Applications

education.area: Computer Science Engineering - AI and Sensor Fusion

publications.name: Le MuMo JEPA: Multi-Modal Self-Supervised Representation Learning with Learnable Fusion Tokens
publications.publisher: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) Workshops - URVIS
publications.summary: A self-supervised framework that learns unified representations from RGB images and aligned companion modalities. Extends LeJEPA to the multi-modal setting by learning fusion tokens that act as a latent bottleneck between modality-specific patch stems inside a shared transformer.

publications.name: In-Field Mapping of Grape Yield and Quality with Illumination-Invariant Deep Learning
publications.summary: Development of the LISA framework for illumination-invariant hyperspectral imaging analysis in precision viticulture. An end-to-end IoT-enabled robotic system for non-destructive, real-time mapping of grape yield and quality.

publications.name: Adaptive Clustering for Efficient Phenotype Segmentation of UAV Hyperspectral Data
publications.publisher: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV) Workshops
publications.summary: Introduction of the OHSLIC algorithm for computationally efficient, real-time phenotype segmentation from hyperspectral imaging data. Enables on-device processing on UAVs.

publications.name: Computational Fairness in Adaptive Neural Networks
publications.summary: A novel investigation into the fairness of adaptive neural networks, analyzing disparities in computational resource allocation across demographic subgroups. Introduces computational resource allocation as a new dimension of AI fairness.
